object_description: two multiply bent volumes of staggered heights forming a courtyard-like ensemble
design_condition: the two bent volumes create a courtyard-like ensemble that ties into the front area of the neighbouring care centre and zones an open space system around them

positive: The free geometries give the school a high degree of independence and its own identity in the neighbourhood
The courtyard-like ensemble ties in with the existing front area of the care centre and forms a clear address
An elegantly zoned open space system combines public and school outdoor spaces into a convincing whole
The playing field is integrated into the park-like green belt
The playground is a visual extension of the parking area between the two buildings
The curved path reinforces the atmosphere and yet gives logical direct access to all elements
The forecourt has an address-forming design and opens up to the adjacent neighbourhood
It has the potential to become a neighbourhood meeting point beyond its school function
A quiet, high-quality recreation and spectator zone is created between pitch, hall and care centre
The split-level layout organises one cluster per floor around a freely formulated access zone
A varied, angled landscape for movement and learning is created with views spanning several storeys
Library and teacher areas are spatially differentiated towards a contemplative inner courtyard
Canteen and multi-purpose hall are grouped around a high foyer lit by a courtyard
This foyer is to a certain extent the social centre of the building
Precise fulfilment of the room programme and appropriate materialisation suggest low construction costs
The project offers high spatial qualities and atmospherically convincing interior worlds
A refreshing proposal, adequate in scale from the perspective of primary school children, with high identification potential
negative: The all-weather pitch restricts the passage of the green space
The resulting jump in height requires a major intervention in the topography with walls and steps
The trees towards the neighbouring site are very dense and permeability should be improved
The forecourt design should be sharpened in line with the square typology
The placement of the school garden at the main entrance does not do justice to the context
The bicycle parking should be examined for a position closer to the main entrance
The circulation area is very tightly dimensioned and can hardly serve as a recreational area
Access to the handicraft rooms and the sports building is somewhat inferior
Compactness and the comparatively large facade area leave something to be desired ecologically
The effect of the building on the outside was strongly questioned
The geometric deflections sometimes appear arbitrary in parts of the ensemble
